outcome: No progress on either stated conjecture was found since 26 January 2024; nearby-sounding results found in searches (Guth–Maynard 2024 zero-density theorem, an arXiv paper titled "On the Second Hardy-Littlewood Conjecture", and a "Simple Proof of the Hardy–Littlewood Conjecture") all concern different problems that merely share the Hardy–Littlewood name or general zeta/prime-counting subject matter.
summary: The Hardy–Littlewood zeta-function conjectures, as stated in the frozen Wikipedia revision, are two specific quantitative claims about zeros of ζ(1/2+it): (1) for H = T^(0.25+ε), the interval (T, T+H] contains a zero of odd order for T large enough; (2) for H = T^(0.5+ε), N₀(T+H) − N₀(T) ≥ cH for T large enough, where N₀ counts zeros on the critical line. Pre-2024 history is well documented (Selberg 1942 proved a weaker exponent result with an extra log T factor; Selberg conjectured the exponent could drop below 1/2; Karatsuba proved this in 1984 and extended it to 'supershort' intervals in 1992; Moser 2014 gave a 16.6% improvement of a related exponent) but none of this is post-January-2024. I searched extensively for anything published since the frozen date that bears on either exact statement (H, c, N₀(T+H)−N₀(T), or odd-order real zeros in short intervals) and found nothing. Three items surfaced repeatedly in search but are false positives on inspection: (a) Guth and Maynard's May 2024 zero-density theorem (arXiv:2405.20552, published in Annals of Mathematics 2026) improves the Ingham bound on N(σ,T) for zeros with σ > 1/2 (off the critical line) — a genuinely major advance, but it addresses a different zero-density question than the Hardy–Littlewood conjectures, which concern the density of zeros ON the critical line (N₀(T)); (b) 'On the Second Hardy-Littlewood Conjecture' (arXiv:2503.02766, March 2025) is about the completely unrelated additive/subadditive conjecture π(x+y) ≤ π(x) + π(y) for the prime-counting function — a namesake collision, not a case or variant of the zeta-zero conjecture; (c) 'Simple Proof of the Hardy–Littlewood Conjecture' (Annals of Mathematics and Physics, June 2025) addresses yet another Hardy–Littlewood conjecture, an additive/Goldbach-type prime representation claim, published in a low-quality open-access journal (Peertechz) and explicitly incomplete (relies on an unproven auxiliary conjecture). A 2026 arXiv preprint ('Jacob's ladders and the equivalent of the Fermat-Wiles theorem generated by the Hardy-Littlewood formula (1921)', arXiv:2603.01747) invokes the 1921 Hardy–Littlewood zeta paper but does not address either stated conjecture and belongs to a long-running, non-mainstream 'Jacob's ladder' series. No AI system appears anywhere in this search: none of the located papers or the Wikipedia article's history mention AI-assisted derivation, and my own broader search for AI mathematical breakthroughs in this period (Erdős problems solved by Gemini/AlphaEvolve-style systems, GPT-5.5 Pro on Borsuk's conjecture, etc.) turned up nothing connected to Hardy–Littlewood zeta zero density or real-zero-gap questions. I am satisfied this is a well-evidenced 'nothing happened' case: the search covered the exact quantities named in the conjectures (H, c, N₀), the general subject (zero density / real zeros of zeta), the Selberg/Karatsuba lineage, and an AI-specific sweep, all with no hits.
competing_reading: One could argue Guth–Maynard's improvement of the Ingham zero-density bound is 'the kind of thing' the triage or a careless reader might fold into 'zero-density progress on zeta' and thus into this bullet as `progress`. But the stated conjectures are specifically about N₀(T) (real zeros on the critical line) and the length of intervals guaranteed to contain such zeros; Guth–Maynard bounds N(σ,T) for σ strictly greater than 1/2, a disjoint quantity. Under §3.1 this is a related problem sharing a subject (zeta zero-counting) rather than a case of the problem as stated, so it does not count as a change to this bullet.
what_would_settle_it: A paper specifically improving the exponent 0.25 in the odd-order-zero conjecture, the exponent 0.5 or the constant c in the N₀(T+H)−N₀(T) ≥ cH conjecture, or a full resolution of either, dated after 26 January 2024, would settle this differently. None was found.
